credit.name: Will Cook, OpenAI Math Atlas; source manuscripts and Lean quotations credited to OpenAI.

rows.label: Exact equality of deterministic and randomized logarithmic space

value.scope:
The formalization proves $\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}$ for binary languages in an explicit Turing-machine model with logarithmic workspace. The randomized classes use polynomial time: $\mathsf{RL}$ never accepts a no-instance and accepts a yes-instance with probability at least $1/2$, while $\mathsf{BPL}$ has acceptance probability at least $2/3$ on yes-instances and at most $1/3$ on no-instances. Thus bounded-error randomness does not enlarge deterministic logarithmic space in this model.

The selected theorem asserts equality of the language classes. The paper's explicit compiler and numerical running-time bounds are not separately stated in this Comparator target.
value.title: Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: $`\mathsf L=\mathsf{RL}=\mathsf{BPL}`$

provenance.rule: Projection of the pinned ledger; no new mathematical assessment.

reader_comparison.method: Compare reported scope categories; notes remain attributed and are not adjudicated.

points.gap: The effective compiler and its explicit polynomial running-time bounds (headline's second sentence) are not stated; only the class equality is.

points.definitions_to_check: Word / Language: languages are sets of binary words (List Bool) only; the paper does not fix the alphabet in its Section 1, so the reduction from larger alphabets is a routine encoding step, not a restriction on the class. ; Machine / Action / Configuration: finite transition-table machine with q+1 states, w two-way-infinite binary work tapes (blank = false) and h read-only two-way input heads, with q, w, h chosen existentially; standard, and matches the paper's 'finite control, endmarked read-only input, finitely many work tapes' model (introduction.tex:10-15). ; Machine.step / run: one fresh coin bit per step (coins t used at step t+1), halting states are fixed points; matches 'fresh independent fair bits' and cannot reuse a past coin except via finite control. ; Machine.LogSpace: space = number of distinct cells visited by each work head up to time t, summed over tapes, bounded by c * Nat.clog 2 (|x|+2) for every input, every coin tape and every time t; standard counted-cell convention (blank-cell visits count), same as the paper. ; Machine.Decides: for every x some time t with all coin tapes halted with output b and (b = true <-> x in A); no explicit time bound is imposed on L-machines (polynomial time follows from the configuration count, as the paper notes at introduction.tex:20-22); standard. ; Machine.HaltsBy: halting by the clock on EVERY coin tape (worst-case time), as the paper requires ('All randomized running-time bounds hold on every random tape'); standard. ; Machine.acceptanceProbability: exact fraction of the 2^t coin strings of length t (padded with false) whose time-t state outputs true, with t = polynomialClock c k |x| = c*(|x|+2)^k; standard. ; RL / BPL: thresholds are exactly 0 on no and >= 1/2 on yes (RL), <= 1/3 on no and >= 2/3 on yes (BPL), as in introduction.tex:22-26; standard.
points.note: Lean states `L = RL ∧ RL = BPL` for binary languages in an explicit multi-head, multi-tape logspace Turing-machine model (one fresh coin per step, polynomial clock on every coin tape, RL = 0 / >= 1/2, BPL = <= 1/3 / >= 2/3), which is the paper's Theorem (introduction.tex:28-32) after unfolding L, RL, BPL and chaining the two equalities; the binary-alphabet convention is the only routine step. The summary's second sentence (effective compiler with explicit polynomial running-time bounds, compiler.tex:8-19) has no Lean statement, as the scope note says.

statements.name: Acceptance-probability approximation
statements.text:
\label{thm:probability}
Fix a randomized machine $\mathcal M$ with polynomial worst-case
running time and $O(\log(n+2))$ work space. Let $p_{\mathcal M}(x)$ be
its acceptance probability on an input $x$ of length $n$. There is a
uniform deterministic algorithm which, on input $(x,1^q)$ with $q\ge1$,
outputs an integer $0\le a\le2^{q+2}$ satisfying
\[
       \left|a2^{-(q+2)}-p_{\mathcal M}(x)\right|\le2^{-q}.
\]
It uses $O(\log(n+2)+q)$ work space and
$(n+2)^{O(1)}2^{O(q)}$ time. The constants depend only on $\mathcal M$.
